description: Model error or rejection rates differ materially across customer groups because training data is unrepresentative or historically skewed (M1, M2, M3).
control: Group-level performance and fairness testing before go-live and each release; documented data provenance and coverage; go-live gate on group error gaps; manual onboarding route for poorly served groups.

description: Proxy features (location, device, network, language, name patterns) reproduce discrimination without using protected attributes.
control: Feature proxy-risk review per release; multi-metric fairness testing; protected attributes held for audit only under restricted access; independent review of feature set.

description: Excessive collection, retention or reuse of biometric and financial data; unauthorised access.
control: Data minimisation and retention schedule; biometric templates separated and encrypted; purpose limitation; data protection impact assessment before launch; role-based access with audit logs.

description: Customers and staff cannot understand or contest AI-informed decisions.
control: Plain-language reason codes for every adverse decision; AI-use notice; documented appeal route with named reviewer and response target; decision logs allowing reconstruction.

description: Reviewers accept model outputs by default (automation bias), so oversight exists only on paper.
control: Monitor override rates and time-per-case; reviewer training; authority and time to override without penalty; mandatory documented human determination for severe or hard-to-reverse outcomes.

description: False positives block or freeze legitimate customers, concentrated on already-flagged groups, with slow or no remedy.
control: Graduated responses (step-up checks, temporary limits) before freezes; dispute resolution target with fast track for essential access; false-positive rate by group as a standing governance metric.

description: Model drift and feedback loops: fraud patterns change, and flagged cases are fed back as training labels, degrading accuracy and amplifying bias.
control: Scheduled drift and performance monitoring with alert thresholds; label-quality review before retraining; retraining under change control with re-run fairness tests.

description: Compromise of the biometric store or models, or attacks on identity checks (spoofed or synthetic faces, document forgery).
control: Liveness and anti-spoofing checks tested regularly; encryption at rest and in transit; penetration testing of the platform and models; security incident runbook linked to AI incident escalation.

description: Dependency on external identity databases, cloud services or pre-trained components that fail, change, or carry their own bias or legal risk.
control: Third-party due diligence and contract clauses (audit, incident notice, data location); fallback procedure if a provider fails; document third-party components in the system inventory.

description: Failure to identify when binding obligations apply (Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023; EU AI Act if the EU trigger is met), including cross-border data transfers.
control: Legal applicability register maintained per market; compliance review as a launch gate for each jurisdiction; legal sign-off on classification of each module (see Task 3).

description: Unclear ownership and slow escalation when the system causes harm, so incidents are not contained or communicated.
control: Defined incident severity levels and escalation path; named accountable executive; authority and procedure to suspend or deactivate the system; communication to affected customers.

description: Staff operating or overseeing the system lack the AI literacy to use outputs responsibly.
control: Role-based training on system limits, bias and oversight duties; competence check before reviewers get access; annual refresh.
